source.title: Understanding Jailbreak Success: A Study of Latent Space Dynamics in Large Language Models
source.authors: Sarah Ball; Frauke Kreuter; Nina Rimsky

record.file_problem: None; the full paper and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether harmfulness-related difference-in-means directions and their activation patterns relate to refusal and jailbreak success, using harmfulness cosine measurements and steering rather than the original study's full refusal-direction ablation procedure.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports extensive transfer and induction results using vectors contrasted between jailbreak and non-jailbreak versions of the same request (Tables 2–8). Those vectors are not the harmful-minus-harmless refusal direction at issue here, so those results are not recorded as rows for these claim versions.
record.test_reason: The 'harmfulness vector' is a harmful-minus-harmless mean difference at the end-of-instruction token, essentially the original's refusal-direction recipe. The study adds it to induce refusal (V1, addition only, qualitative) and measures whether successful jailbreaks lower activation cosine with it (V3, correlational). There is no ablation, weight edit, or adversarial training.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that vectors built from jailbreak versus non-jailbreak prompts share a common component. Subtracting them mitigates jailbreaks across classes, including GCG, and adding them induces jailbreaks. Effective jailbreaks noticeably reduce the represented prompt harmfulness in most models. The size of that reduction does not clearly map to ASR, so suppression may not be the only mechanism, and the analysis is correlational.
record.recipe_differences: Uses mean-difference activations to construct a harmfulness direction and demonstrates refusal induction by activation steering, but does not perform the original study's systematic removal of one refusal direction across layers and positions or test retained capabilities.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported reduction varies by model: it is strongest for Vicuna 13B and significantly less pronounced for MPT 7B. The alternative harmfulness measurement gives similar conclusions with less pronounced reduction overall, except for MPT 7B.

fits_no_version.finding: Vectors contrasting jailbreak and non-jailbreak versions of the same request share cosine of about 0.4–0.6 across classes. Subtracting them cuts ASR on other classes from 100% to near 0, versus 56–71% with a random vector (Table 2). Adding them induces jailbreaks at up to about 93% ASR (Table 3).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Semantically distinct jailbreak types share a common activation component whose removal restores refusal.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference of the European Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics (2024); the text also labels itself preprint under review.
record.problems: The harmfulness-suppression evidence is correlational and the authors state that it does not establish a causal relationship. The reported cosine values are shown in figures without numerical values in the text. Refusal induction on harmless questions is illustrated with qualitative examples rather than a reported rate. The paper notes less pronounced harmfulness reduction for MPT 7B.
record.rows_left_out: Results for jailbreak-derived contrast vectors steering against or inducing jailbreaks (Tables 2–8) are not included: those vectors contrast jailbreak and non-jailbreak versions of the same request, rather than the harmful-minus-harmless direction or the refusal direction named in the versions tested here.

untested.parts: Directional ablation removing refusal on harmful prompts; refusal-induction rates rather than examples; preservation of general capabilities.
Causal test that attacks work via the direction; training against its ablation for robustness.
No separate harmfulness versus refusal representations are extracted. The authors' mismatched-generalization explanation is speculative.

missing.what: Repeat of the suppression analysis with an alternative harmfulness direction averaged over all instruction tokens. It reaches similar conclusions with less pronounced reduction, except in MPT 7B.
Token-level cosine traces: with no jailbreak, the end-of-instruction cosine is high and the response is a refusal; jailbroken examples show reduced end-of-instruction cosine across all four models.

record.verdict_notes: The 'harmfulness direction' here is constructed like the original's refusal direction, so V1 and V3 links are kept. However, the authors interpret it as harm perception, and that framing does not test V5. V1 evidence is four single examples with unstated steering parameters. ASR is judged by Llama 3 8B and Llama Guard 2. Peer-review status is unclear: the text is a 'preprint under review' (v2, Oct 2024).

versions.untested_parts: Does not ablate the direction, test projection at every layer and position, quantify removal of refusal, or measure preservation of general capabilities.
No weight-edit or released-model abliteration experiment.
Does not causally test whether attacks suppress the original refusal direction, or whether training against its ablation adds robustness.
Does not compare affine, cone, or multiple refusal-direction accounts.
Does not establish a causal or independently decoded separation between harmfulness judgment and refusal decision.
No test of the refusal direction's transfer across languages, model variants, or base and instruct models.
No comparison of refusal-training procedures or training stages.

relation.reason: Section 5.4 reports its own measurements of whether effective jailbreaks suppress the harmful-minus-harmless direction across 4 models.

tranche.reason: The direction is a paired harmful-minus-harmless (ChatGPT-rewritten) mean difference at the last instruction token, at a fixed middle layer with no validation selection. The study measures how 25 jailbreak types change cosine with it. That is the same question as V3 with a related but not identical recipe, so T2 is defensible. It is close to T1 because the original's suffix analysis also used cosine.

source_check.notes: Nina Panickssery co-authors both this study and the original (Arditi et al. 2024), so it is not fully independent. All harmfulness-cosine results are figure-only. The alternative all-token direction weakens the reduction for every model except MPT 7B (Fig 15). The pack's review field says EACL 2024, but the text is v2 (Oct 2024) marked 'Preprint under review'. The only 'ignore all the instructions' text is a quoted dev_mode_v2 jailbreak prompt, which doesn't count.

statements.correction: 2406.09289: successful template and GCG jailbreaks lower end-of-instruction cosine with a harmful-minus-harmless mean-difference direction in most of 4 chat models (Vicuna 7B/13B v1.5, Qwen1.5 14B, MPT 7B). The drop is strongest in Vicuna 13B. Values are figure-only (Fig 7). Preprint under review, code available, correlational by the authors' own statement.
statements.problem: Cites r5 from this study, but neither the 'what' nor the 'why' names or describes any 2406.09289 result. A reader can't trace the cited row.

statements.correction: Qwen1.5 14B evil_confidant: harmfulness reduction 'seems less pronounced' (Fig 7, no value stated); ASR 96.88% (Table 1, Llama 3 + Llama Guard, 352 questions). MPT 7B: 'significantly less harmfulness reduction'. Discussion: no clear mapping between suppression size and ASR.
statements.problem: 'Little suppression' overstates the text. For Qwen evil_confidant the text only says the reduction 'seems less pronounced'; the value is figure-only. The other parts are right.
None. Section 6 cites the study's 'correlational perspective' and says further work must establish whether the relationship is causal.

statements.correction: Could add: with the all-token-average harmfulness direction, reduction is less pronounced for all models except MPT 7B (Fig 15, figure-only).
statements.problem: Correct: reduction is 'strongest for the Vicuna 13B model' and 'significantly less' for MPT 7B. It omits that with the alternative all-token direction, reduction is less pronounced for all models except MPT 7B (Fig 15), so the model contrast depends on how the direction is built.

No specific claim about this study. Listing Vicuna and Qwen among families with lower projection under attack is consistent with it. This study shares an author (Nina Panickssery) with the original Arditi et al. 2024, so it is likely the one counted in tested_sharing_an_author_with_an_original = 1 (count not verifiable here).
